CURRICULUM · 12 WEEKS
The beginner path

A chronological journey from your first straight cut to a finished side table. Twelve weeks, twelve small kits, three checkpoints. Each kit ships with pre-milled stock, a printed plan, and the exact tools you'll need next — no guesswork, no half-bought toolboxes.

Cutting

Finishing

W01
CUTTING
The honest pine coaster set

Learn to make a square cut you can trust. Four coasters by Friday — and a feel for grain direction.

YOU'LL LEARN
Reading grain and choosing the show face
Marking a square line with a try square
Making a straight crosscut with a pull saw
Pull saw, try square

W02
CUTTING
Beveled bread board

Move from square cuts to angled ones. Your first chamfer, your first plane shaving, and a board you'll actually use.

YOU'LL LEARN
Setting up and reading a block plane
Cutting a 45° chamfer freehand
Sanding through grits 120 → 220
Block plane, sanding block
2 hrs
$32
Add kit
W03
CUTTING
Notched key rack

Practice the saw-and-chisel rhythm that underlies every joint you'll cut for the rest of your life.

YOU'LL LEARN
Layout with a marking gauge
Chopping a stopped notch with a chisel
Paring down to a knife line
1/2" chisel, marking gauge
2.5 hrs
$38
Add kit
03
04
W04
CUTTING
Tapered plant stand legs

Your first compound cuts. Four matching tapers — a small obsession with consistency begins here.

YOU'LL LEARN
Building a simple taper jig
Matching four parts to a single reference
Easing edges with a card scraper
Card scraper, dovetail saw
3 hrs
$42
Add kit
CHECKPOINT · W04
You can cut. Cleanly.

Four kits in, you've moved from square cuts to compound tapers. Before joining anything together, take an evening to drill the basics until they feel boring.

SKILLS YOU SHOULD OWN
Straight crosscuts to a knife line
Setting and using a block plane
Chopping a notch in three strokes
Sanding without flat spots or swirls
Download practice sheet — Cut-list drills (PDF, 4 pp)
Printable mark-up template — Try-square calibration
YOU'RE READY FOR…

Joining — putting two pieces of wood together so they stay that way. Starts week 5.

W05
JOINING
Doweled photo frame

Your first hidden joint. Six dowels, four corners, and a frame that's stronger than it looks.

YOU'LL LEARN
Drilling straight, stopped holes
Using a doweling jig for alignment
Clamping a four-corner glue-up
Hand drill, doweling jig
2.5 hrs
$36
Add kit
05
06
W06
JOINING
Lap-jointed wall shelf

A half-lap is the friendliest joint in woodworking. By Sunday, you'll have cut six of them.

YOU'LL LEARN
Marking a half-lap to a mating piece
Sawing on the waste side of the line
Fitting with a router plane
Router plane, mallet
3 hrs
$48
Add kit
W07
JOINING
Mortise-and-tenon stool top

The joint that built every chair you've ever sat in. Four mortises, four tenons, one stool top.

YOU'LL LEARN
Chopping a clean through-mortise
Sawing a tenon's four shoulders
Test-fitting and paring for a snug seat
Mortise chisel, marking knife
3.5 hrs
$56
Add kit
07
08
W08
JOINING
Through-dovetailed box

The joint everyone is afraid of, made approachable. Pre-milled stock with the layout already gauged.

YOU'LL LEARN
Laying out tails-first dovetails
Sawing to a line at an angle
Transferring pin sockets cleanly
Dovetail saw, fishtail chisel
4 hrs
$58
Add kit
CHECKPOINT · W08
You can join wood to wood.

Halfway through. You've cut, doweled, lapped, mortised and dovetailed. Now the work shifts from "does it hold?" to "does it look like you meant it?"

SKILLS YOU SHOULD OWN
Reading a joint before you cut it
Cutting on the waste side, every time
A four-corner glue-up under 8 minutes
Recovering from a slightly fat tenon
Download practice sheet — Joint sampler (PDF, 6 pp)
Printable dovetail layout template — 1:7 angle
YOU'RE READY FOR…

Finishing — the four weeks that take a project from "made it" to "kept it." Starts week 9.

W09
FINISHING
Oiled cutting board

The simplest finish in the book, done properly. Three coats, two days, one board you'll use weekly.

YOU'LL LEARN
Raising and knocking back the grain
Applying mineral oil and beeswax
Knowing when a board is "done"
Oil, wax, lint-free rag
2 hrs over 2 days
$34
Add kit
09
10
W10
FINISHING
Shellac-finished trinket box

Your first film finish. Padded on, not brushed. The result is a warm, glassy surface you wouldn't believe you made.

YOU'LL LEARN
Cutting your own shellac from flake
Padding on thin, even coats
Rubbing out to a satin sheen
Shellac flake, denatured alcohol
3 hrs
$44
Add kit
W11
FINISHING
Stained oak desk caddy

Stain is a craft, not a paint job. Learn to control colour without losing the grain underneath.

YOU'LL LEARN
Conditioning open-grain hardwoods
Wiping stain on, off, and even
Topcoating with wipe-on poly
Stain, conditioner, poly
3.5 hrs
$52
Add kit
11
12
W12
CAPSTONE
The tapered side table

Everything together. Tapered legs (W04), mortise-and-tenon aprons (W07), an oiled top (W09). Twelve weeks ends with furniture.

YOU'LL LEARN
Sequencing a multi-stage glue-up
Attaching a top with shop-made buttons
Final-finishing a piece of furniture
All previous tools, four bar clamps
6 hrs over 2 weekends
$118
Add kit
CHECKPOINT · W12 — GRADUATION
You finished the path.

Twelve weeks, twelve completed projects, one piece of furniture you'll keep. The whole curriculum fits in a shoebox of tools and lives in your head now.

SKILLS YOU SHOULD OWN
Reading a plan and ordering operations
Three reliable joints: dowel, lap, M&T
Oil, shellac, and stain-plus-poly finishing
Assembling and finishing a piece of furniture
Download practice sheet — Capstone cut list (PDF, 8 pp)
Printable certificate — Beginner Path, completed
YOU'RE READY FOR…

The Intermediate Path — hand-cut joinery, drawer-making, and your first chair. Launches spring.
